chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Pop Henry's, the Sterling Hotel in Cincinnati and Jerry the rat
summary: In Cincinnati they ate at Pop Henry's near the Sterling Hotel, where an old rat named Jerry roamed the halls.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Name another. Do you remember --
Then there was Pop Henry's in
Cincinnati.
Uncle Henry, yeah.
Yeah. That was a pitch till you win.
That was around the corner from the Sterling Hotel. That's where we all stayed.
That's right, uh-huh. It was around on Fifth Street -- No, Fifth or Third. Third Street? I think it was on Third Street because the Sterling Hotel was at Sixth and Mound.
Sixth and Mound.
Yeah, because I lived there when I first went there.
That's where all the black musicians -- that was a black hotel.
That's right.
You remember there was a rat there that everybody used to talk about?
Jerry.
Jerry.
Jerry was so old until the hair was off his back. He used to shed the hair off his back sliding in and out of them holes, we used to say all the time.
And everybody just knew Jerry, this great rat, he was so old.
Oh, sure, yeah.
Tell us about that.

And Jerry would -- they had these trash cans in the hall, you know. Everybody would put their garbage out there. Jerry would know and Jerry would walk down the hall besides you and didn't pay you no mind. He'd walk right on by you and go to his trash can and leap up there and try to get what he wanted out of there. And nobody paid Jerry any attention. Nobody was scared of him. He didn't bite nobody. He didn't bother nobody, you know.
It's hard to tell people that, but so many musicians of our era know that Jerry used to walk up and down those halls. This rat was big as any cat we ever saw.
